claim: Nsp5 is the main protease of SARS-CoV-2 that cleaves viral polyproteins into individual polypeptides necessary for viral replication.
source: Nonstructural protein 5 (Nsp5) is the main protease of SARS-CoV-2 that cleaves viral polyproteins into individual polypeptides necessary for viral replication.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about SARS-CoV-2 biology.

claim: Nsp5 binds and cleaves human tRNA methyltransferase 1 (TRMT1).
source: Here, we show that Nsp5 binds and cleaves human tRNA methyltransferase 1 (TRMT1), a host enzyme required for a prevalent post-transcriptional modification in tRNAs.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data showing interaction and cleavage of TRMT1 by Nsp5.

claim: TRMT1 is a host enzyme required for a prevalent post-transcriptional modification in tRNAs.
source: Here, we show that Nsp5 binds and cleaves human tRNA methyltransferase 1 (TRMT1), a host enzyme required for a prevalent post-transcriptional modification in tRNAs.
evidence: This is established knowledge about TRMT1 function, also supported by citations in the manuscript.

claim: Human cells infected with SARS-CoV-2 exhibit a decrease in TRMT1 protein levels.
source: Human cells infected with SARS-CoV-2 exhibit a decrease in TRMT1 protein levels and TRMT1-catalyzed tRNA modifications, consistent with TRMT1 cleavage and inactivation by Nsp5.
evidence: The manuscript presents immunoblot data showing reduced TRMT1 levels in infected cells.

claim: Human cells infected with SARS-CoV-2 exhibit a decrease in TRMT1-catalyzed tRNA modifications.
source: Human cells infected with SARS-CoV-2 exhibit a decrease in TRMT1 protein levels and TRMT1-catalyzed tRNA modifications, consistent with TRMT1 cleavage and inactivation by Nsp5.
evidence: The manuscript presents mass spectrometry data showing reduced m2,2G modification levels in infected cells.

claim: Nsp5 cleaves TRMT1 at a specific position that matches the consensus sequence of SARS-CoV-2 polyprotein cleavage sites.
source: Nsp5 cleaves TRMT1 at a specific position that matches the consensus sequence of SARS-CoV-2 polyprotein cleavage sites, and a single mutation within the sequence inhibits Nsp5-dependent proteolysis of TRMT1.
evidence: The manuscript presents sequence analysis and experimental data showing site-specific cleavage.

claim: A single mutation within the cleavage sequence inhibits Nsp5-dependent proteolysis of TRMT1.
source: Nsp5 cleaves TRMT1 at a specific position that matches the consensus sequence of SARS-CoV-2 polyprotein cleavage sites, and a single mutation within the sequence inhibits Nsp5-dependent proteolysis of TRMT1.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data showing that Q530N mutation prevents cleavage.

claim: The TRMT1 cleavage fragments exhibit altered RNA binding activity.
source: The TRMT1 cleavage fragments exhibit altered RNA binding activity and are unable to rescue tRNA modification in TRMT1-deficient human cells.
evidence: The manuscript presents RNA binding assays showing differential binding by TRMT1 fragments.

claim: The TRMT1 cleavage fragments are unable to rescue tRNA modification in TRMT1-deficient human cells.
source: The TRMT1 cleavage fragments exhibit altered RNA binding activity and are unable to rescue tRNA modification in TRMT1-deficient human cells.
evidence: The manuscript presents primer extension assays showing lack of rescue by TRMT1 fragments.

claim: TRMT1-deficient human cells infected with SARS-CoV-2 exhibit reduced levels of intracellular viral RNA compared to wild-type human cells.
source: Compared to wild-type human cells, TRMT1-deficient human cells infected with SARS-CoV-2 exhibit reduced levels of intracellular viral RNA.
evidence: The manuscript presents qRT-PCR data showing reduced viral RNA in TRMT1-KO cells.

claim: Nsp5-dependent cleavage of TRMT1 and perturbation of tRNA modification patterns contribute to the cellular pathogenesis of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
source: These findings provide evidence that Nsp5-dependent cleavage of TRMT1 and perturbation of tRNA modification patterns contribute to the cellular pathogenesis of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: SARS-CoV-2 is an enveloped, single-stranded RNA virus that is the causative agent of the COVID-19 pandemic.
source: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) is an enveloped, single-stranded RNA virus that is the causative agent of the COVID-19 pandemic (Lamers and Haagmans, 2022; Merad et al., 2022).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: SARS-CoV-2 is a member of the Betacoronavirus genus of the Coronaviridae family.
source: SARS-CoV-2 is a member of the Betacoronavirus genus of the Coronaviridae family, which includes the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 1 (SARS-CoV-1) and Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) (reviewed in Hartenian et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established taxonomic knowledge supported by citation.

claim: SARS-CoV-2 primarily targets the human respiratory tract and lungs.
source: SARS-CoV-2 primarily targets the human respiratory tract and lungs, which can clinically manifest as an acute respiratory distress syndrome.
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge about SARS-CoV-2 infection.

claim: The incoming positive-strand viral RNA genome is first translated by host ribosomes into two overlapping polyproteins, pp1a and pp1ab.
source: Once delivered into the host cell, the incoming positive-strand viral RNA genome is first translated by host ribosomes into two overlapping polyproteins, pp1a and pp1ab.
evidence: This is established knowledge about SARS-CoV-2 replication cycle.

claim: Viral polyproteins are proteolytically processed into 16 mature nonstructural proteins (Nsps) involved in the assembly of the viral replication-transcription complex.
source: Viral polyproteins are then proteolytically processed into 16 mature nonstructural proteins (Nsps) involved in the assembly of the viral replication-transcription complex (reviewed in V'kovski et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The Nsps participate in disrupting host cellular processes and pathways to escape immune recognition and facilitate viral propagation.
source: The Nsps also participate in disrupting host cellular processes and pathways to escape immune recognition and facilitate viral propagation (reviewed in Minkoff and tenOever, 2023; Suryawanshi et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The maturation step to release the individual Nsp polypeptides is executed by two viral-encoded proteases: Nsp5 and Nsp3.
source: The maturation step to release the individual Nsp polypeptides is executed by two viral-encoded proteases: Nsp5 (also known as Main Protease, MPro/3C-like protease) and Nsp3 (also known as Papain-Like Protease, PLPro) (Narayanan et al., 2022).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Nsp3 is contained within pp1a and releases itself from the polyprotein through self-cleavage.
source: Nsp3 is contained within pp1a and releases itself from the polyprotein through self-cleavage.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Nsp3 function.

claim: Nsp3 cleaves pp1a at multiple sites to release Nsp1 through Nsp4.
source: Nsp3 also cleaves pp1a at multiple sites to release Nsp1 through Nsp4 (Yan and Wu, 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The Nsp5 main protease processes pp1b at eleven sites to release itself and Nsp4 to Nsp16.
source: The Nsp5 main protease processes pp1b at eleven sites to release itself and Nsp4 to Nsp16 (Chen et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Nsp3 and Nsp5 have been found to cleave endogenous host proteins linked to the immune response and cell survival.
source: Besides cleaving viral substrates, Nsp3 and Nsp5 have also been found to cleave endogenous host proteins linked to the immune response and cell survival (Liu et al., 2021; Meyer et al., 2021; Meyers et al., 2021; Moustaqil et al., 2021; Wenzel et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2021b).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Nsp3 and Nsp5 are essential for viral replication and represent well-characterized drug targets among coronaviruses.
source: Nsp3 and Nsp5 are essential for viral replication and represent well-characterized drug targets among coronaviruses.
evidence: This is established knowledge about coronavirus biology and drug development.

claim: The active component of the antiviral drug Paxlovid is nirmatrelvir, a reversible covalent inhibitor of the Nsp5 main protease.
source: Notably, the active component of the antiviral drug Paxlovid is nirmatrelvir, a reversible covalent inhibitor of the Nsp5 main protease (Owen et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Paxlovid reduces viral replication and disease severity in patients with COVID-19 by inhibiting Nsp5 proteolytic activity.
source: By inhibiting Nsp5 proteolytic activity, Paxlovid reduces viral replication and disease severity in patients with COVID-19.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Paxlovid's mechanism and clinical effects.

claim: Purification of individual SARS-CoV-2 proteins from human cells identified a potential interaction between a catalytic-inactive version of Nsp5 with human TRMT1.
source: Purification of individual SARS-CoV-2 proteins from human cells have identified a potential interaction between a catalytic-inactive version of Nsp5 with human TRMT1 (Gordon et al., 2020a).
evidence: This is prior work cited from the literature.

claim: TRMT1 interacts with a catalytic-inactive version of Nsp5 encoded by SARS-CoV-1, which is 98.7% similar to SARS-CoV-2.
source: A cross-coronavirus investigation from the same group has extended this observation by finding that TRMT1 interacts with a catalytic-inactive version of Nsp5 encoded by SARS-CoV-1, which is 98.7% similar to SARS-CoV-2 (Gordon et al., 2020b).
evidence: This is prior work cited from the literature.

claim: No detectable interaction was found between TRMT1 and Nsp5 encoded by MERS-CoV, which has 66.8% similarity with SARS-CoV-2.
source: Interestingly, the same study found no detectable interaction between TRMT1 and Nsp5 encoded by MERS-CoV, which has 66.8% similarity with SARS-CoV-2.
evidence: This is prior work cited from the literature.

claim: TRMT1 was identified as a potential interactor with catalytic-inactive Nsp5 using proximity-dependent biotinylation.
source: TRMT1 was also identified as a potential interactor with catalytic-inactive Nsp5 using proximity-dependent biotinylation (Samavarchi-Tehrani et al., 2020).
evidence: This is prior work cited from the literature.

claim: TRMT1 catalyzes the formation of dimethylguanosine (m2,2G) at position 26 in more than half of all human tRNAs.
source: TRMT1 is a tRNA modification enzyme that catalyzes the formation of dimethylguanosine (m2,2G) at position 26 in more than half of all human tRNAs (Dewe et al., 2017; Jonkhout et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The m2,2G modification is located at a key structural position in tRNAs and is hypothesized to play a role in proper tRNA folding.
source: The m2,2G modification is located at a key structural position in tRNAs and is hypothesized to play a role in proper tRNA folding (Pallan et al., 2008; Steinberg and Cedergren, 1995).
evidence: This is established knowledge and hypothesis supported by citations.

claim: TRMT1-deficient human cells exhibit perturbations in global protein synthesis and decreased proliferation.
source: TRMT1-deficient human cells exhibit perturbations in global protein synthesis and decreased proliferation (Dewe et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Loss-of-function variants in the TRMT1 gene are the cause of certain types of intellectual disability disorders in humans.
source: Moreover, loss-of-function variants in the TRMT1 gene are the cause of certain types of intellectual disability disorders in humans (Blaesius et al., 2018; Najmabadi et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Changes in TRMT1 activity can impact protein synthesis leading to downstream cellular and biological effects.
source: Thus, changes in TRMT1 activity can impact protein synthesis leading to downstream cellular and biological effects.
evidence: This is an inference based on established knowledge about TRMT1 function.

claim: Retroviruses such as HIV use cellular tRNAs as primers for reverse transcription and other viral functions.
source: In one well-known example, retroviruses such as HIV use cellular tRNAs as primers for reverse transcription and other viral functions (reviewed in Jin and Musier-Forsyth, 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: DNA and RNA viruses can impact tRNA synthesis, processing, and charging to modulate infection and pathogenesis.
source: DNA and RNA viruses can also impact tRNA synthesis, processing, and charging to modulate infection and pathogenesis (Dremel et al., 2022; Netzer et al., 2009; Tucker et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Chikungunya RNA virus infection increases the expression of a human tRNA modification enzyme and alters tRNA modification patterns to favor viral protein expression.
source: In a recent study, Chikungunya RNA virus infection has been shown to increase the expression of a human tRNA modification enzyme and alter tRNA modification patterns to favor viral protein expression (Jungfleisch et al., 2022).
evidence: This is prior work cited from the literature.

claim: SARS-CoV-2 viral particles exhibit an enrichment of specific host tRNAs with distinct modification profiles.
source: Interestingly, SARS-CoV-2 viral particles exhibit an enrichment of specific host tRNAs with distinct modification profiles (Peña et al., 2022).
evidence: This is prior work cited from the literature.

claim: Analysis of RNA extracted from human nose swabs identified tRNA profiles and modification signatures associated with mild versus severe COVID-19.
source: Moreover, analysis of RNA extracted from human nose swabs have identified tRNA profiles and modification signatures associated with mild versus severe COVID-19 (Katanski et al., 2022).
evidence: This is prior work cited from the literature.

claim: MRC-5 cells infected with SARS-CoV-2 exhibited a ~30% reduction in TRMT1 levels at 24- and 48 hr post-infection compared to mock-infected cells.
source: In multiple independent replicates, MRC-5 cells infected with SARS-CoV-2 exhibited a ~30% reduction in TRMT1 levels at 24- and 48 hr post-infection compared to mock-infected cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: The manuscript presents quantified immunoblot data showing this reduction.

claim: m2,2G levels were decreased by ~15% at 48 hr post-infection in SARS-CoV-2-infected cells compared to mock-infected cells.
source: While m2,2G levels did not exhibit a significant change between mock-infected and SARS-CoV-2-infected cells at 24 hr post-infection, m2,2G levels were decreased by ~15% at 48 hr post-infection in multiple biological replicates (Figure 1C).
evidence: The manuscript presents mass spectrometry data showing this decrease.

claim: More than half of all tested RNA modifications exhibited a decrease in SARS-CoV-2-infected cells compared to mock-infected cells at 24 hr post-infection.
source: In addition to m2,2G, more than half of all tested RNA modifications exhibited a decrease in SARS-CoV-2-infected cells compared to mock-infected cells at 24 hr post-infection (Figure 1D).
evidence: The manuscript presents mass spectrometry data showing changes in multiple RNA modifications.

claim: At 48 hr post-infection with SARS-CoV-2, most of the tested RNA modifications exhibited a decrease in levels compared to mock-infected cells.
source: At 48 hr post-infection with SARS-CoV-2, most of the tested RNA modifications exhibited a decrease in levels compared to mock-infected cells.
evidence: The manuscript presents mass spectrometry data showing this trend.

claim: Human TRMT1 contains an eight amino acid residue sequence between the methyltransferase domain and zinc-finger motif matching the consensus sequence of Nsp5 cleavage sites in SARS-CoV-2 polyproteins.
source: Examination of the primary structure of human TRMT1 revealed an eight amino acid residue sequence between the methyltransferase domain and zinc-finger motif matching the consensus sequence of Nsp5 cleavage sites in SARS-CoV-2 polyproteins (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: The manuscript presents sequence analysis showing this match.

claim: The putative cleavage site in TRMT1 includes a glutamine (Q) residue conserved at the fourth position that is found in all Nsp5 cleavage sites of SARS-CoV-2 polyproteins.
source: The putative cleavage site in TRMT1 includes a glutamine (Q) residue conserved at the fourth position that is found in all Nsp5 cleavage sites of SARS-CoV-2 polyproteins (Figure 2B).
evidence: The manuscript presents sequence analysis showing this conservation.

claim: The putative Nsp5 cleavage site in TRMT1 is expected to lie in an unstructured linker region exposed on the surface of TRMT1 based on Alpha Fold prediction.
source: Based upon a predicted tertiary structure of TRMT1 using Alpha Fold (Jumper et al., 2021; Varadi et al., 2022), this putative Nsp5 cleavage site is expected to lie in an unstructured linker region exposed on the surface of TRMT1 (Figure 2C).
evidence: The manuscript presents structural prediction data.

claim: Endogenous TRMT1 was enriched in the purification with Nsp5-C145A.
source: In contrast, endogenous TRMT1 was enriched in the purification with Nsp5-C145A (Figure 2D, TRMT1 high exposure, lane 9).
evidence: The manuscript presents protein purification data showing this enrichment.

claim: TRMT1-FLAG was detected specifically in the Nsp5-C145A purification compared to the control or Nsp5 purifications.
source: TRMT1-FLAG was also detected specifically in the Nsp5-C145A purification compared to the control or Nsp5 purifications (Figure 2D, compare lanes 10 and 11 to lane 12).
evidence: The manuscript presents protein purification data showing this specific detection.

claim: Nsp5 can interact with TRMT1 when Nsp5 is in the catalytic-inactive form.
source: These results provide evidence that Nsp5 can interact with TRMT1 when Nsp5 is in the catalytic-inactive form.
evidence: This is an inference from the purification data showing interaction with Nsp5-C145A.

claim: Cleavage after amino acid residue 530 of TRMT1 is predicted to result in an N-terminal fragment of 58 kDa and a C-terminal fragment of 14 kDa.
source: Cleavage after amino acid residue 530 of TRMT1 is predicted to result in an N-terminal fragment of 58 kDa and a C-terminal fragment of 14 kDa.
evidence: This is a calculation based on the predicted cleavage site and protein sequence.

claim: Lysates prepared from human cells expressing Nsp5 exhibited an additional band migrating below the non-specific band that matches the predicted size of the N-terminal TRMT1 fragment.
source: However, lysates prepared from human cells expressing Nsp5 exhibited an additional band migrating below the non-specific band that matches the predicted size of the N-terminal TRMT1 fragment (Figure 3B, TRMT1, lanes 4–6, arrow).
evidence: The manuscript presents immunoblot data showing this band.

claim: The putative N-terminal TRMT1 fragment was detectable at 24 hr post-transfection with the Nsp5-expression plasmid, increased at 48 hr, and remained detectable at 72 hr post-transfection.
source: The putative N-terminal TRMT1 fragment was detectable at 24 hr post-transfection with the Nsp5-expression plasmid, increased at 48 hr, and remained detectable at 72 hr post-transfection (Figure 3B).
evidence: The manuscript presents time-course immunoblot data.

claim: The N-terminal TRMT1 fragment was not detected above the background signal in human cells expressing the proteolytically inactive Nsp5-C145A mutant.
source: In contrast, the N-terminal TRMT1 fragment was not detected above the background signal in human cells expressing the proteolytically inactive Nsp5-C145A mutant (Figure 3B, TRMT1, lanes 7–9, quantified in 3 C).
evidence: The manuscript presents immunoblot data showing absence of cleavage with Nsp5-C145A.

claim: A ~20 kDa product matching the expected molecular weight of a FLAG-tagged C-terminal TRMT1 cleavage product was detected in the lysate of human cells expressing Nsp5 but not vector alone or Nsp5-C145A.
source: In addition, using an antibody against the FLAG tag, we could detect a ~20 kDa product matching the expected molecular weight of a FLAG-tagged C-terminal TRMT1 cleavage product in the lysate of human cells expressing Nsp5 but not vector alone or Nsp5-C145A (Figure 4A, FLAG, arrowhead).
evidence: The manuscript presents immunoblot data showing the C-terminal fragment.

claim: SARS-CoV-2 Nsp5 cleaves at the predicted cleavage site in TRMT1 leading to N- and C-terminal fragments in human cells.
source: These data provide evidence that SARS-CoV-2 Nsp5 cleaves at the predicted cleavage site in TRMT1 leading to N- and C-terminal fragments in human cells.
evidence: This is an inference from the detection of both N- and C-terminal fragments.

claim: All Nsp5 cleavage sites in SARS-CoV-1 and SARS-CoV-2 polyproteins contain a glutamine residue at position four.
source: All Nsp5 cleavage sites in SARS-CoV-1 and SARS-CoV-2 polyproteins contain a glutamine residue at position four (Figure 2B; Grum-Tokars et al., 2008; Jin et al., 2022; Lee et al., 2022).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations and sequence analysis.

claim: Mutation of the glutamine to asparagine is sufficient to abolish recognition and cleavage by Nsp5 from SARS-CoV-1 or SARS-CoV-2.
source: Mutation of the glutamine to asparagine is sufficient to abolish recognition and cleavage by Nsp5 from SARS-CoV-1 or SARS-CoV-2 (Heilmann et al., 2022; Muramatsu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The appearance of the N- or C-terminal TRMT1 cleavage fragments was barely detectable when the TRMT1-Q530N mutant was co-expressed with Nsp5.
source: In contrast to wild-type TRMT1, the appearance of the N- or C-terminal TRMT1 cleavage fragments was barely detectable when the TRMT1-Q530N mutant was co-expressed with Nsp5 (Figure 4C, lane 8, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The manuscript presents immunoblot data showing lack of cleavage with Q530N mutation.

claim: TRMT1 can be recognized and cleaved by Nsp5 in human cells with cleavage requiring a sequence that matches Nsp5 cleavage sites in SARS-CoV-2 polyproteins.
source: Altogether, these results demonstrate that TRMT1 can be recognized and cleaved by Nsp5 in human cells with cleavage requiring a sequence that matches Nsp5 cleavage sites in SARS-CoV-2 polyproteins.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mutagenesis and cleavage experiments.

claim: TRMT1 exhibits a stable interaction with rRNAs and substrate tRNAs that are targets for m2,2G modification.
source: We have previously shown that TRMT1 exhibits a stable interaction with rRNAs and substrate tRNAs that are targets for m2,2G modification (Dewe et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is prior work from the authors' lab supported by citations.

claim: The purification of full-length TRMT1 resulted in the enrichment of rRNA and tRNAs compared to the control purification from vector-transfected cells.
source: As expected, the purification of full-length TRMT1 resulted in the enrichment of rRNA and tRNAs compared to the control purification from vector-transfected cells (Figure 5C, compare lane 6 to lane 7).
evidence: The manuscript presents RNA purification data showing this enrichment.

claim: The Q530N variant of TRMT1 exhibited comparable binding of tRNAs as full-length TRMT1.
source: The Q530N variant of TRMT1 also exhibited comparable binding of tRNAs as full-length TRMT1 (Figure 5C, lane 10).
evidence: The manuscript presents RNA purification data showing comparable binding.

claim: No detectable enrichment of rRNA or tRNA was detected for the N-terminal TRMT1 fragment.
source: In contrast, no detectable enrichment of rRNA or tRNA was detected for the N-terminal TRMT1 fragment (Figure 5C, lane 8).
evidence: The manuscript presents RNA purification data showing lack of enrichment.

claim: The N-terminal TRMT1 cleavage fragment appears to be insufficient for binding tRNA while the C-terminal fragment containing the Zn-finger motif is sufficient for binding to tRNAs.
source: Thus, the N-terminal TRMT1 cleavage fragment appears to be insufficient for binding tRNA while the C-terminal fragment containing the Zn-finger motif is sufficient for binding to tRNAs.
evidence: This is an inference from the RNA binding data.

claim: Re‐expression of full-length TRMT1 or TRMT1-Q530N in the TRMT1‐KO cell line was able to restore m2,2G formation in both tRNA-Met-CAU and mt-tRNA-Ile-UAU.
source: Re‐expression of full-length TRMT1 or TRMT1-Q530N in the TRMT1‐KO cell line was able to restore m2,2G formation in both tRNA-Met-CAU and mt-tRNA-Ile-UAU (Figure 5E, lanes 7 and 9).
evidence: The manuscript presents primer extension data showing rescue of modification.

claim: Neither the N- nor C-terminal TRMT1 fragment was able to restore m2,2G formation in the tRNAs of the TRMT1‐KO cell line.
source: However, neither the N- nor C-terminal TRMT1 fragment was able to restore m2,2G formation in the tRNAs of the TRMT1‐KO cell line (Figure 5E, lanes 8 and 10).
evidence: The manuscript presents primer extension data showing lack of rescue.

claim: Cleavage of TRMT1 by Nsp5 leads to protein fragments that are inactive for tRNA modification activity.
source: These results indicate that cleavage of TRMT1 by Nsp5 leads to protein fragments that are inactive for tRNA modification activity.
evidence: This is an inference from the functional rescue experiments.

claim: Full-length TRMT1-GFP exhibited cytoplasmic localization along with a punctate signal in the nucleus.
source: Full-length TRMT1-GFP exhibited cytoplasmic localization along with a punctate signal in the nucleus (Figure 5—figure supplement 1, TRMT1-WT, GFP).
evidence: The manuscript presents microscopy data showing this localization pattern.

claim: The fluorescence signal for TRMT1 in the cytoplasm overlapped partially with the RFP-tagged mitochondrial marker.
source: The fluorescence signal for TRMT1 in the cytoplasm overlapped partially with the RFP-tagged mitochondrial marker (Figure 5—figure supplement 1, Merge, yellow signal).
evidence: The manuscript presents microscopy data showing this overlap.

claim: The N-terminal TRMT1 fragment exhibited primarily cytoplasmic localization with a greatly reduced signal in the nucleus.
source: The N-terminal TRMT1 fragment exhibited primarily cytoplasmic localization with a greatly reduced signal in the nucleus, consistent with a lack of the nuclear localization signal at the C-terminus (Figure 5—figure supplement 1, TRMT1 N-term, GFP, merge).
evidence: The manuscript presents microscopy data showing this localization pattern.

claim: The C-terminal TRMT1 fragment displayed primarily nuclear localization with very little signal in the cytoplasm.
source: In contrast to the N-terminal TRMT1 fragment, the C-terminal TRMT1 fragment displayed primarily nuclear localization with very little signal in the cytoplasm (Figure 5—figure supplement 1, TRMT1 C-term, GFP, merge).
evidence: The manuscript presents microscopy data showing this localization pattern.

claim: TRMT1 in the cytoplasm is the likely target of Nsp5 cleavage with the cleavage fragments displaying altered localization compared to full-length TRMT1.
source: These results suggest that TRMT1 in the cytoplasm is the likely target of Nsp5 cleavage with the cleavage fragments displaying altered localization compared to full-length TRMT1.
evidence: This is an inference from the localization data.

claim: TRMT1 protein levels decreased in the TRMT1-KO cell lines expressing TRMT1-WT after infection with SARS-CoV-2 compared to mock-infection.
source: Compared to mock-infection, TRMT1 protein levels decreased in the TRMT1-KO cell lines expressing TRMT1-WT after infection with SARS-CoV-2 (Figure 7A, lanes 1–3; quantified in 7B).
evidence: The manuscript presents immunoblot data showing this decrease.

claim: The level of TRMT1 was not appreciably changed in the TRMT1-KO cell line expressing TRMT1-Q530N after infection with SARS-CoV-2.
source: Notably, the level of TRMT1 was not appreciably changed in the TRMT1-KO cell line expressing TRMT1-Q530N after infection with SARS-CoV-2 (Figure 7A, lanes 4–6; quantified in 7 C).
evidence: The manuscript presents immunoblot data showing stable TRMT1-Q530N levels.

claim: The decrease in endogenous TRMT1 levels after SARS-CoV-2 infection is due to cleavage of TRMT1 by Nsp5.
source: These results provide evidence that the decrease in endogenous TRMT1 levels after SARS-CoV-2 infection is due to cleavage of TRMT1 by Nsp5.
evidence: This is an inference from the comparison of TRMT1-WT and TRMT1-Q530N stability during infection.

claim: TRMT1-KO cells exhibited a ~three to fourfold reduction in viral RNA compared to control cells infected at the same MOI.
source: Notably, TRMT1-KO cells exhibited a ~three to fourfold reduction in viral RNA compared to control cells infected at the same MOI (Figure 6E and F).
evidence: The manuscript presents qRT-PCR data showing this reduction.

claim: Expression of TRMT1 is necessary for efficient SARS-CoV-2 replication in human cells.
source: These results suggest that expression of TRMT1 is necessary for efficient SARS-CoV-2 replication in human cells.
evidence: This is an inference from the reduced viral RNA in TRMT1-KO cells.

claim: TRMT1-KO cell lines re-expressing TRMT1 exhibited higher viral RNA production relative to the TRMT1-KO+vector cell line that was comparable to the control-WT cells.
source: TRMT1-KO cell lines re-expressing TRMT1 exhibited higher viral RNA production relative to the TRMT1-KO+vector cell line that was comparable to the control-WT cells (Figure 7D, compare KO +vec to KO +WT).
evidence: The manuscript presents qRT-PCR data showing rescue of viral replication.

claim: The TRMT1-KO cell line expressing TRMT1-Q530N exhibited a higher level of viral RNA production compared to the TRMT1-KO cell line expressing TRMT1-WT at higher MOI.
source: Notably, the TRMT1-KO cell line expressing TRMT1-Q530N exhibited a higher level of viral RNA production compared to the TRMT1-KO cell line expressing TRMT1-WT at higher MOI (Figure 7, KO +Q530 N).
evidence: The manuscript presents qRT-PCR data showing enhanced replication with non-cleavable TRMT1.

claim: The presence or absence of TRMT1 impacts SARS-CoV-2 RNA production in human 293T cells.
source: Since the presence or absence of TRMT1 appears to impact SARS-CoV-2 RNA production in human 293T cells, we tested if this phenomenon could alter viral particle production.
evidence: This is an inference from the viral RNA quantification experiments.

claim: The supernatant from infected TRMT1-KO cells exhibited reduced titer and slightly lower infectivity when compared to viral particles produced from control-WT cells.
source: Consistent with the reduced levels of viral RNA in TRMT1-KO cells infected with SARS-CoV-2, the supernatant from infected TRMT1-KO cells exhibited reduced titer and slightly lower infectivity when compared to viral particles produced from control-WT cells (Figure 8, control-WT versus TRMT1-KO).
evidence: The manuscript presents viral titer and infectivity data.

claim: Re-expression of TRMT1 in the TRMT1-KO cells partially restored viral titer at the lower MOI and increased infectivity compared to supernatants from TRMT1-KO cell lines.
source: Re-expression of TRMT1 in the TRMT1-KO cells partially restored viral titer at the lower MOI and increased infectivity compared to supernatants from TRMT1-KO cell lines (Figure 8, TRMT1-KO+vec versus TRMT1-KO+WT).
evidence: The manuscript presents viral titer and infectivity data showing partial rescue.

claim: The expression of the non-cleavable TRMT1-Q530N variant in TRMT1-KO cells promoted an increase of viral titer as well as infectivity compared to expression of wild-type TRMT1.
source: Interestingly, the expression of the non-cleavable TRMT1-Q530N variant in TRMT1-KO cells promoted an increase of viral titer as well as infectivity compared to expression of wild-type TRMT1 (Figure 8, TRMT1-KO+WT versus TRMT1-KO+Q530 N).
evidence: The manuscript presents viral titer and infectivity data showing enhanced production with non-cleavable TRMT1.

claim: TRMT1 expression plays a role in virus production and the generation of optimally infectious SARS-CoV-2 particles.
source: Altogether, these observations suggest an unexpected role for TRMT1 expression in virus production and the generation of optimally infectious SARS-CoV-2 particles.
evidence: This is an inference from the viral titer and infectivity experiments.

claim: TRMT1 is an endogenous cleavage target of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease.
source: Here, we demonstrate that TRMT1 tRNA modification enzyme is an endogenous cleavage target of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the manuscript supported by multiple experiments.

claim: D'Oliviera et al. have determined the structural basis for recognition of TRMT1 by the SARS-CoV-2 main protease, which has revealed a distinct binding mode for certain substrates of the main protease, including TRMT1.
